canonical_name: Pointer copy with an exact identity key
plain_what: When asked 'what is Ana's locker?', the model should copy the stored answer from earlier text rather than invent one. The pointer chooses which earlier token to copy. This mechanism wants it to choose by the exact name of the slot (Ana plus locker), not by the surrounding wording. Measured today, the pointer instead lands on the repeated sentence frame.
how_it_works: The copy head mixes a copy distribution into the output: p = (1-g)*softmax(z) + g * sum over sources j with token x_j = v of a_j, where g is a learned gate and a_j is the pointer's attention over a window of earlier tokens. The project-specific part is how a source is chosen. Every token has a registered prime; a source is admitted when gcd with the query's atoms is above 1, or by ordered n-let equality (RouteAdmission::SharedAtom or Ngram); rarer atoms weigh more (ln gcd); the route score is scaled by ROUTE_SHARPNESS = 4.0 and the attention is a softmax over admitted sources. A token-identity term (PointerIdentity) adds the overlap of the six tokens before the source with the six before the query (POINTER_IDENTITY_WINDOW = 6). A fixed table folds case and one leading space to a canonical id (copy_identity.rs); it only decides matches and never changes the emitted token. The intended key is the slot address (entity prime times attribute prime), not the wording around the value. Export serves only an unrouted, unselected pointer; the identity and routed variants are offline.
geometry: Prime atoms with gcd and ordered n-let admission (ADR-0003 prime router, ln-gcd weighting); a fixed token-id fold table. No Hopf, E8 or quaternion object is used by the pointer itself.

status_reason: Every tested form is a softmax pointer in a dense float stack that missed its bar or cannot be served: a real prime-ranked key raised the dev hit rate 0.377 to 0.5452 yet memory stayed 19/21/23 vs 20/40 (docs/labs/ptr-addr-2026-10-10/README.md); export refuses identity terms. The entity-address key and forced-copy oracle were never run.
reopen_conditions: Run the serving-time forced-copy oracle first (supply the true slot address or span; the copy-span oracle instrument exists but N/O1/O2 on the bound artifact were never run, docs/labs/copy-span-oracle-2026-10-12/README.md) to bound the gain at no training cost.

Then a parsed or learned slot-address key (entity prime times attribute prime) trained in from the start of the dialogue fine-tune, with matched controls, at least 3 seeds and at least 120 memory rows; pre-registered bar of at least +5/40-equivalent over the control.

A copy distribution with no softmax (rank table, hard select, or exact admission plus learned ranking) so the head can be registered under D23/D30, as a new offline float sheet under D37 or on the D32 discrete path, with fresh TEST FITNESS: FIT and owner release.
An integer serving route by gcd or n-let equality with no float score, with the export gap reported.

rule_compat.D11: Export serves only an unrouted, unselected pointer; a pointer carrying an identity term is refused at export (docs/labs/token-identity-stop-open-population-2026-10-09/README.md) and D10 refuses pointer models (docs/integration/direction-review-2026-09-30.md). The fold table is one table read plus integer equality, stated D11-legal in copy_identity.rs.
rule_compat.D23: Violates as built: the mixture uses softmax(z) and the pointer attention is a softmax over admitted sources (geometric_stack.rs, ROUTE_SHARPNESS comment); eras.md era-28 records that it 'used softmax and could not be served'.
rule_compat.D30: The pointer sits inside a dense float stack and its score is a dot product, so it is not matmul-free as built.
rule_compat.D32_D37: Not on the D32 discrete path (no pointer there). D37 permits an offline float re-registration in a separately scanned module with an integer export and reported gap; nothing is released.

ptr-addr one-atom prime route: a raised hit rate with unchanged answers, but the pointer branch carries only about 6 percent of the mixture (answer-path record), so the read-outs measured a minor branch; the bottleneck is after the source is found.
Gate-supervision fine-tune: a control with no supervision reached 22/40, so the result says nothing about the pointer.
Inference-path knobs (TopK(2), floor 0.9) on unchanged weights: a two-setting decode change, not a trained key.
v5 declared acceptance 10/40: the artifact had no memory operator at all.
Span-extraction read-out: a re-tuning of where to start reading the answer, not a key.
